why_this_delta: Current Trigger-2 course records a reproducible unknowable-fact/abstention weakness for the provisional Qwen3.5-0.8B target and requires DB-vs-simulation authority discrimination. External 2025-2026 abstention research additionally indicates that answer correctness and question answerability are separable reliability axes and that reasoning fine-tuning can degrade abstention. Trigger-2 therefore should not collapse epistemic answerability into one confidence/correctness target.

source_evidence.claim: Provisional TARGET_MEASURED had 4/5-seed unknowable-fact fabrication weakness; BASE remains mandatory matched control; DB-vs-simulation authority is load-bearing.
Physical GRID10 and stale-result proof gaps remain blocked from credit; exact executable evidence outranks model consensus.
AbstentionBench reports abstention remains unsolved and reasoning fine-tuning degraded abstention by 24% on average in its evaluated setting.
Two Axes of LLM Abstention reports answer correctness and question answerability behave as distinct axes; hidden-state answerability signals can differ from ordinary answer-confidence.
Variable-binding training can pass through shallow-heuristic phases before systematic binding; this supports shortcut-resistant family-disjoint evaluation rather than surface-label training.

core_hypothesis.hypothesis: For Xeno, ANSWERABILITY and CANDIDATE_CORRECTNESS should be represented/evaluated as separate axes before action realization. A model can be able to produce a plausible or even locally correct-looking candidate while the current evidence state does not authorize a factual answer.
core_hypothesis.counterhypothesis: A single calibrated correctness/confidence target plus explicit UNKNOWN examples is sufficient; a two-axis target adds complexity without independent generalization benefit.
core_hypothesis.falsifier: On family-disjoint held-out cases, compare a one-axis baseline against a two-axis factorized evaluator at matched model/token budget. Reject the two-axis design if it fails to improve unanswerable/false-premise/stale-evidence behavior without harming answerable correctness, DB-vs-simulation authority discrimination, exact-format compliance or low-refusal allowed-task capability.

secondary_hypotheses.hypothesis: Typed runtime evidence states such as CURRENT, STALE_REJECTED and REBASE_PROVEN should condition answerability, while hash/lease/CAS proof remains deterministic-shell authority.
secondary_hypotheses.counterhypothesis: If stale packets are always suppressed before model cognition, explicit stale-conditioned answerability training is unnecessary.
secondary_hypotheses.discriminator: Matched traces with identical semantic task content but different typed runtime state outcomes; score whether Xeno rereads/recomputes instead of inventing freshness.

secondary_hypotheses.hypothesis: False-premise detection and missing-evidence abstention require distinct negative families from broad refusal behavior so low-refusal capability can be retained.
secondary_hypotheses.counterhypothesis: On the provisional low-refusal checkpoint family, epistemic abstention is entangled with refusal suppression and cannot be repaired independently by small targeted data.
secondary_hypotheses.discriminator: Pareto evaluation across unanswerable abstention, false-premise handling, allowed low-refusal tasks, structural reasoning, DB-vs-simulation authority and exact-format compliance. No aggregate score can hide a failed required axis.

proposed_factorization.authority_boundary: Axes and action projection are model/eval candidates only. S0 truth, stale/current/rebase validity, capability and effects remain deterministic boundaries.
